# D2SBtools

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of D2SBtools is to provide helpful internal tools for D2SB projects. 

## Installation

You can install the development version of D2SBtools like so:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
devtools::install_github("petersonR/D2SBtools")
```

Then load the library: 

```{r}
library(D2SBtools)
```


# Example

This is a basic example.

## Create new D2SB project

The following copies the [template project directory](https://github.com/petersonR/D2SBtools/tree/main/inst/templates/project/skeleton) and thereby creates a new project. 

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# This will open a new R session
create_project(
  project_name = "temporary_project", 
  path = NULL, # creates in current directory
  
  # Set parameters in Admin/project.yml (can be done later too)
  title = "My D2SB Project",
  analyst = "Me",
  status = "active",
  pi = "My PI",
  data_path_from_sharepoint = "Projects/template_project"
)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# write a local verson to be able to read
create_project(
  project_name = "temporary_project", 
  path = NULL, # creates in current directory
  open = FALSE, # Opens in RStudio
  
  # Set parameters in Admin/project.yml (can be done later too)
  title = "My D2SB Project",
  analyst = "Me",
  status = "active",
  pi = "My PI",
  data_path_from_sharepoint = "Projects/template_project"
)
fs::dir_copy("temporary_project/Admin", ".")
```


## Get all available project data

Moving into this temporary project, we can then run the following commands

```{r example}
get_project_data()
```

## Get specific project data 

```{r}
get_project_data("title")
```

## Get sharepoint path

```{r}
sp_path()

```

## List files on sharepoint

```{r}
list.files(sp_path())
```

## Read data off sharepoint

```{r}
test_data <- read_csv(sp_path("DataRaw/test_data.csv")) 
test_data
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, include = FALSE}
unlink("temporary_project", recursive = TRUE)
unlink("Admin", recursive = TRUE)
```


## Create new report

A D2SB template report is available via this package. A new report based on this template can be created via: 

```{r, eval = FALSE}
create_report(path = "Reports/new.qmd")
```

## Sign a figure

Every published D2SB figure carries the group's signature: the logo in the
bottom-right corner, at the same physical size and position on every figure.
Pass the size the figure will be saved at, so the placement is right:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, ggplot2::aes(wt, mpg)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point()

ggplot2::ggsave(
  "fig1.tif", add_signature(p, width = 7, height = 5),
  width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 1200, compression = "lzw"
)
```

In a Quarto chunk, use the chunk's `fig-width` and `fig-height`.

## Convert a SQLite database to DuckDB

`db2duckdb()` copies every table into a DuckDB file, checking row counts
table by table, and can be rerun to resume after a crash. On Argon, point
`scratch` at local scratch and size `workers` to the job:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# qsub -cwd -q AML-HM -pe smp 48 -l mf=256G db2duckdb.sh
db2duckdb(
  src = "/Shared/Statepi_Premier/databases/premier_24.db",
  dest = "/Shared/Statepi_Marketscan/databases/premier/premier_24.duckdb",
  scratch = "/localscratch/Users/hawkid",
  workers = 12
)
```

## Log a deliverable

Each project keeps `Admin/products.csv`, a record of everything it has
delivered or plans to deliver. Add to it with `add_product()`; analyst, PI,
date, and id are filled in from `Admin/project.yml`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
add_product(
  type = "figures",
  title = "Manuscript figures 1-3 for journal submission",
  source_file = "Code/make_figures.R",
  related = "VHF-003"
)
```

More examples, one per common deliverable. Put the specifics in `title` and
`notes`, and links to grants or other products in `related`, so `type` stays
countable across projects:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Statement of work at the start of a project
add_product("sow", "Statement of work and timeline",
            source_file = "Admin/SOW.docx")

# Standalone statistical analysis plan for a study, still being written.
# `related` can tag the grant that funds the study.
add_product("sap", "SAP for the primary outcome analysis",
            status = "in_progress", actual_date = NA,
            target_date = "2026-11-15", related = "grant=NIH-R01-2027")

# Comprehensive analysis report sent to the PI
add_product("report", "Comprehensive analysis report v1",
            source_file = "Reports/report_comprehensive.qmd",
            artifact_url = "Dissemination/2026-10-13-report_comprehensive.html",
            notes = "Full results; supersedes the EDA report")

# Revision of that report: a new row, linked to the original
add_product("report", "Comprehensive analysis report v2",
            related = "PROJ-003", notes = "Revised after PI feedback")

# Conference abstract, submitted
add_product("abstract", "IDWeek 2027 abstract", status = "submitted",
            related = "PROJ-003")

# Manuscript, accepted (dates are YYYY-MM-DD strings or Date objects)
add_product("manuscript", "Readiness gaps in VHF preparedness",
            status = "accepted", actual_date = "2027-02-01",
            artifact_url = "https://doi.org/10.xxxx/xxxxx")

# Grant application the project contributed to. An analysis plan or power
# analysis written as a section of the application is part of this product,
# not a separate `sap` row.
add_product("grant", "R01 resubmission", status = "submitted",
            notes = "Wrote the analysis plan and power analysis sections")

# Analysis dataset handed off to the team
add_product("dataset", "Analysis dataset v1 with data dictionary",
            source_file = "Code/run_all.R")
```

When a product's status changes, such as a submitted abstract that is later
accepted, edit `status` (and `actual_date`) in its existing row rather than
adding a new one. One row per product keeps group-wide counts honest, and git
keeps the history. A revision that is delivered separately, like the v2
report above, is a new product and gets its own row.

`product_vocabulary()` lists the types and statuses. A project that still has
`Admin/products_minimal.xlsx` is converted to the CSV the first time
`add_product()` runs.
